title: Delegated Processor: Evidence & Retention Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a repeatable, legally defensible approach for requesting, preserving, and returning evidence from delegated processors (subprocessors) and for documenting retention/deletion actions. It is intended to be used by Security, Legal, and Customer Success when responding to customer audits, regulator inquiries, or internal compliance checks.

Scope:
Applies to all third-party processors that: collect, store, transmit, or process Redwood customer data on behalf of Redwood Inference, including hosted, dedicated, and private deployment partners. Excludes pure utility providers (e.g., office supply vendors) unless they access customer data.

Core principles:
- Minimize scope: request only the smallest set of artifacts necessary for the specific inquiry.
- Chain of custody: capture provenance and handling metadata for every artifact sent to Redwood or a regulator.
- Timebox and SLA: use short deadlines for live incidents, longer for routine audits; track responsiveness.
- Reproducibility: evidence should be machine-readable where possible (logs, hashes, config snapshots).
- Legal bindings: always attach the relevant contract/DPA clause reference when requesting evidence.

Definitions (for playbook use):
- Evidence: logs, configuration exports, access lists, audit reports, encrypted backups, database dumps, retention logs, deletion proofs.
- Preservation hold: temporary suspension of normal deletion/retention cycles for specific data or systems.
- Handback: process for transferring copies of artifacts or attestations back to the customer or their auditor.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Security (request owner): drafts the request, identifies scope, performs technical validation of artifacts.
- Legal: ensures the request and any sample clauses cited are consistent with contract terms and applicable law.
- Vendor Manager: coordinates follow-up, records SLAs, updates vendor risk profile.
- Subprocessor: recipient of the request — required to acknowledge, preserve artifacts, and deliver according to the SLA.

Evidence request workflow (standard):
1) Triage & scope: Security determines which systems/time windows are in scope, lists required artifact types, and assigns severity (routine, elevated, incident).
2) Contract check: Legal confirms whether the contract/DPA gives Redwood the rights requested (audit, evidence, onsite review). If rights are limited, note escalation path.
3) Draft request: Security prepares the evidence request package (see templates below) and references the governing clause and ticket ID.
4) Send & acknowledge: Vendor Manager sends via vendor portal/email with a requirement to acknowledge within 48 hours (24 hours for incidents).
5) Preservation hold: Subprocessor implements hold and confirms preservation actions (timestamped).
6) Delivery: Subprocessor transmits artifacts via agreed secure channel (SFTP, signed S3 URL, encrypted archive with KMS key info).
7) Validation: Security verifies integrity (checksums/hashes), basic completeness, and redacts/flags any PII not relevant to scope.
8) Closure: After validation, evidence is stored in the evidence repository, ticket updated, and retention timers applied.

SLA & timeline guidance:
- Incident (customer-impacting): Acknowledgement within 24 hours; preservation confirmation within 48 hours; initial artifact set delivered within 5 business days.
- Regulatory request / audit: Acknowledgement within 48 hours; preservation confirmation within 5 business days; delivery within 15 business days (or longer if contractually allowed).
- Routine internal compliance checks: Acknowledgement within 5 business days; delivery within 20 business days.

Preservation measures checklist (to request from subprocessor):
- Snapshot of affected system(s) (VM image, container image, DB snapshot) with timestamp.
- Full access logs for servers, application, and relevant orchestration systems covering the relevant window.
- Configuration exports (network ACLs, firewall rules, IAM policies).
- Backup manifests and encryption metadata (which keys, key IDs, rotation history).
- User access list and privilege escalation records for the period.
- Retention & deletion logs demonstrating previous retention rules and last deletion times.

Evidence formats & integrity:
- Preferred: structured logs (JSON/NDJSON), database exports (CSV/SQL with schema), config as text (YAML/JSON), gzipped archives.
- All artifacts must be accompanied by SHA256 checksums.
- If encrypted, vendor must provide key identifiers and a secure method to decrypt for Redwood Security (subject to contract). Avoid sharing plaintext keys over email.

Chain-of-custody template (short):
- Generated by: [system/person]
- Generated at (UTC): [ISO8601 timestamp]
- Export method: [API/DB dump/snapshot]
- File names + checksums: [list]
- Sent to: [redwood recipient email or bucket]
- Transfer method: [SFTP/S3/secure-external-audit-portal]
- Receipt confirmed by: [name] (Redwood) at [timestamp]

Retention & deletion verification (contractual clauses to use where needed):
- Retention schedule snippet (for inclusion as exhibit):
  * System logs and debug traces: retained for 90 days by default; can be extended to 365 days upon customer request.
  * Customer production data: retained per customer instruction; default retention 30 days post-termination unless otherwise agreed.
  * Backups: retained for 90 days; backup snapshots containing customer data are subject to same deletion obligations.

- Deletion verification process (operational):
  1. Subprocessor runs deletion job and generates deletion manifest (recording objects deleted, job id, timestamp).
  2. Subprocessor provides manifest + storage-level tombstone metadata + deletion logs.
  3. Security validates by sampling object ids and confirming absence (via API) and checks snapshot history.
  4. Subprocessor issues signed attestation of deletion (see attestation clause below).

Sample modular contract language (short snippets to paste into DPAs or Statements of Work):
- Preservation & Access: "Upon receipt of a reasonable evidence request, Processor shall: (a) acknowledge within the time period set forth in the Agreement; (b) preserve relevant systems and data; and (c) provide timely access to evidence via secure transfer mechanisms. Processor shall maintain chain-of-custody documentation for all evidence produced."
- Deletion attestation: "Processor shall provide a verifiable deletion manifest within 10 business days of execution of a deletion request. The manifest shall include object identifiers, timestamps, and verification hashes, and shall be signed by an authorized officer of the Processor."
- Subprocessor cooperation: "Processor shall enforce these obligations downstream to any Subprocessor and shall provide evidence of such enforcement upon request."

Sample evidence request email (template):
Subject: Evidence Request — [Customer] — Ticket #[ID]
Hi [Vendor contact],
Please treat this request as an official preservation and evidence request under our Agreement (ref: DPA §X.Y). Scope: [brief scope]. Required artifacts: [list]. Please acknowledge receipt within 48 hours and confirm preservation actions. Delivery channel: [SFTP / signed S3 URL]. Ticket: [link].
Thanks,
[Name], Redwood Security

Sensitive data handling & redaction guidance:
- If artifacts include customer PII or third-party personal data, subprocessor should redact or provide minimized extracts unless unredacted data is explicitly necessary and permitted by contract/regulation.
- Security may request an encrypted, isolated review environment if unredacted data is essential for remediation.

Audit readiness checklist (for vendor onboarding & periodic reviews):
- Evidence request contact and escalation list on file.
- Evidence transfer mechanisms validated (test transfer completed in last 90 days).
- Preservation-hold procedure documented and tested.
- Deletion attestation template available and signed by an officer.
- Retention schedule mapped against customer data types.

Record retention for Redwood internal records:
- Evidence repository: retained for 7 years for contractual/regulatory matters unless otherwise prohibited.
- Preservation logs and chain-of-custody: retained for 7 years.
- Attestations and signed manifests: retained indefinitely as part of the contract record.

Escalation & remediation:
- If a subprocessor fails to comply within SLA, Vendor Manager must escalate to Legal within 48 hours.
- Legal evaluates remedies (contractual performance cure, service credits, termination right) and notices vendor of contractual breach.

Appendix A — Recommended deliverable checklist by scenario:
- Live incident (high): system snapshot, full access logs, recent deployments, privilege escalation trail, encryption key metadata, immediate PII extracts as needed.
- Post-incident diagnostic: sanitized trace logs, timeline of actions, remediation steps taken.
- Audit (regulatory/customer): exports covering agreed date ranges, policy default snapshots, signed attestations for deletion/retention.

Appendix B — Example attestation wording (to request from vendor):
"I, [name], [title] of [Processor], attest that the artifacts described in the attached deletion manifest were securely deleted on [date] in accordance with the deletion procedures described in the Agreement. I further attest that to the best of my knowledge the deletion was completed and no recoverable copies remain in production storage systems."

Notes & open questions (for next review):
- Should Redwood standardize a single signed S3+KMS flow for evidence delivery to reduce ad hoc approaches?
- Clarify permitted redaction rules per region (EU data protection vs. US regulators).
- Add a short template for on-prem customer auditors to access preserved artifacts under supervised review.

End of playbook.

Document history: Drafted by Maya Chen (Security) 2025-11-15. Major revisions 2026-02-20 to tighten SLA language and add preservation checklist.
